solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Called off dance, sadly having little room inside (9)

indicators.note: a dance done sadly is done badly, so its letters come out in a jumbled order
the jumbled dance has, or holds, the next piece within it
the little room is placed inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: DANCE rearranged; it opens after its third letter to take the next piece
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

annotation.surface: An event is scrapped, and the dance crammed into a tiny room was a sorry affair anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: Little room is a stock crossword phrase for a cell, the kind a monk or prisoner lives in.
annotation.definitionFit: An event that is scrapped or abandoned before it happens has been called off.

clue.text: Pussy protecting old fur? (4)

indicators.note: the cat wraps around the next piece as if guarding it

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

annotation.surface: A cat guarding a moth-eaten fur, with the question mark admitting the picture is odd.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that fur is being asked for loosely: the definition is an animal's hairy covering.
annotation.definitionFit: The hairy covering that grows over an animal's body, like a cat's own, is called its fur.

clue.text: Normal sort of note (7)

blocks.note: in written music, a note that is neither sharp nor flat

annotation.walkthrough: In written music a sign cancels an earlier sharp or flat, and the note it marks takes the same name as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Unforced, expected behaviour is normal; in music the word also names a plain note carrying neither sharp nor flat.

clue.text: Work unit in Chester garden (3)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the last two letters of Chester and the first of garden

annotation.surface: A job-creation scheme or piece of work set in a garden in Chester, an English city.
annotation.walkthrough: Chester, an English city, is only there to supply letters across the gap into garden.
annotation.definitionFit: Physicists measure energy and work in several units, and this small one belongs to the old centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Spreading calumny, losing millions is madness (6)

indicators.note: the letters of calumny are spread about into a new order
calumny loses something, so the letter standing for millions is taken away before the rearranging

blocks.note: the fodder, a word meaning slander
M = million(s); take it out to leave CALUNY

annotation.surface: Spreading slander, even at the cost of millions, is a crazy thing to do.
annotation.walkthrough: Spreading reads as spreading gossip, which is what calumny is, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: The word once blamed insanity on the moon's phases, and survives as a plain synonym for madness or wild folly.

clue.text: Mac dieted wrongly — reduced by 10 per cent (9)

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: Mac went on the wrong diet and ended up losing a tenth of his weight.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the strict historical sense: the Roman army punished a mutinous unit by killing one soldier in ten.
annotation.definitionFit: Roman commanders punished mutiny by executing one soldier in every ten, the original sense before the word came to mean destroyed.

clue.text: Metal container (3)

blocks.note: a can or box for food

annotation.walkthrough: It reads as one thing, a metal container, but splits into two separate definitions of the same word.
annotation.definitionFit: The silvery element used for plating is a metal, and a can of beans or biscuits is a container.

clue.text: School term’s beginning with wet weather (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of term is its first letter

annotation.surface: The school term starts, as it so often does, in the rain.
annotation.walkthrough: School looks like a noun beside term, but here it is the verb, as in schooling a horse.
annotation.definitionFit: To school a horse or pupil is to teach and drill them in a skill.

clue.text: Goddess arranged mise en scène originally (7)

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order
scène is used only as it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of scène, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A theatre director has set out the staging, the mise en scène, for a play about a goddess.
annotation.walkthrough: Mise en scène is the French term for how a stage or film scene is arranged, so arranged sits naturally beside it.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the deity of retribution, punishing arrogance and undeserved good fortune.

clue.text: Somehow get Nina something to fight disease (7)

indicators.note: the letters come together in some other order

annotation.surface: Someone must find a way to get Nina a remedy for her illness.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is kept vague as something because the answer strictly triggers the immune response rather than fighting disease itself.
annotation.definitionFit: It is a substance that prompts the body's immune system to produce antibodies, which then attack infection.

clue.text: Appeal first to cause damage (5)

indicators.note: what comes first to cause is its opening letter

annotation.surface: A court appeal that sets out to do damage from the start.
annotation.walkthrough: Appeal suggests a legal appeal, but it is the noun meaning attractiveness.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone with appeal has an attractive, winning quality that draws people to them.

clue.text: The last word in forecasts in difficult situations (12)

indicators.note: the last word goes inside forecasts

blocks.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

annotation.surface: The final say in weather forecasts about bad conditions.
annotation.walkthrough: The last word reads as the final say in an argument, but it is the word that ends a prayer.
annotation.definitionFit: Awkward, tricky plights that are hard to escape from are difficult situations.

clue.text: Spotting some Parisian in tears (9)

annotation.surface: Catching sight of a Parisian who is weeping.
annotation.walkthrough: Parisian points to French: des means some.
annotation.definitionFit: Descry is an old literary verb for catching sight of something distant, which is spotting it.

clue.text: Harry is secret agent, very holy person (6)

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

annotation.surface: A man called Harry turns out to be a spy and a saint at once.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to harass or pester them persistently, the older sense of the answer.

clue.text: Outside one church mum meets the Spanish saint (7)

indicators.note: mum goes around one church, standing outside it
the Spanish word joins on after, meeting the rest

annotation.surface: Mum, outside a church, runs into a Spanish saint.
annotation.walkthrough: Mum splits around one church, so the M and A are not together in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The archangel who defeats the dragon in Revelation is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Doesn’t move bits of wood (6)

blocks.note: stays put, as a jammed drawer does
twigs or cut lengths of timber

annotation.surface: Pieces of wood lying still.
annotation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of motionless wood, but the verb and the plural noun are two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: A jammed drawer stays put and so doesn't move; twigs gathered for a fire are bits of wood.

clue.text: Vehicle I purchased — not half a beast! (7)

indicators.note: only half of bought is used

blocks.note: BOUGHT with its second half (GHT) dropped

annotation.surface: A buyer complains that the car they purchased is a beast of a machine.
annotation.walkthrough: Not half sounds like the British exclamation meaning very much so, but here it removes half of bought.
annotation.definitionFit: This North American reindeer is a large wild animal, and beast is a crossword's general word for any animal.

clue.text: One insect or another that will die ultimately (6)

definitions.note: another stands for another insect, leaning on the insect named first

indicators.note: take the last letter of each of the three words before it

blocks.note: last letters of thaT wilL diE

annotation.surface: A gloomy note on insect life: every one of them will die in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Another means another insect: the definition leans on the first insect in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: The answer is a hard-winged creature, so it is a second insect alongside the bee.

clue.text: Church always needs top people who will encourage others? (12)

definitions.note: people is shared: it ends top people and also heads the definition, people who will encourage others

blocks.note: e'er, the poetic contraction of ever

annotation.surface: A church will always need people at the top to lead the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic form of ever, meaning always. The question mark admits the definition is a cheeky description.
annotation.definitionFit: Their job at sports games is to whip up the crowd and rally the team, urging others on.

clue.text: Aloof, hiding head? Show feelings dramatically (5)

indicators.note: the first letter is kept out of sight

annotation.surface: A distant person hiding their face, then bursting into theatrical displays of feeling.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether an aloof person would hide their head, but the head is a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Actors who overplay their parts, with exaggerated gestures and expressions, are said to do this.

clue.text: Garment in love story (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of love and the first two of story

annotation.surface: A piece of clothing that features in a romance.
annotation.walkthrough: Love tempts the solver to use O, but the answer runs across the join of love and story.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain it is a sleeveless undershirt, in America a waistcoat; either way an item of clothing.

clue.text: Excellent new form of oil, a dressing (5)

indicators.note: oil is given a new arrangement

blocks.note: A1 = excellent, with the 1 written as I

annotation.surface: A cook praises a new kind of oil-based salad dressing.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, and crosswords often read the digit 1 as the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: It is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence, spooned over fish and vegetables as a sauce.

clue.text: Shake maiden overcome by huge drink (7)

indicators.note: the maiden is swallowed up by the drink

blocks.note: a treble is a triple measure of spirits
M = maiden, the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over with no runs

annotation.surface: A young woman is floored by an enormous drink and starts to shake.
annotation.walkthrough: In a pub a treble is a triple measure of spirits, hence huge drink. M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: To quiver or shudder involuntarily, from fear or cold, is to shake.

clue.text: Consume beef, say, sliced off on top (3)

indicators.note: the first letter is cut away, as in a down clue its top

blocks.note: beef is an example of meat, which is what say signals

annotation.surface: Eat some beef that has been carved from the top of the joint.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Swallowing food as a meal is how we consume it.

clue.text: Not all sleep in shelter (3)

indicators.note: only part of sleep is used
the answer lies within the word

blocks.note: the middle three letters of sleep

annotation.surface: Some of the night's sleep is taken under cover.
annotation.walkthrough: In is doing double duty as a word of the surface, but it also marks where the letters sit.
annotation.definitionFit: The side of a hill or ship turned away from the wind is sheltered, so sailors speak of its cover.

clue.text: Rage uncontrollably and provoke female relation (5-4)

indicators.note: the letters of rage run wild into a new order

annotation.surface: An elderly relative flies into a fury and goads the family.
annotation.walkthrough: The join between the two pieces falls one letter away from the hyphen, so the answer only appears when they are run together.
annotation.definitionFit: Your grandmother's sister, or your parent's aunt, is a female relation.
